rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a CrN diffusion barrier layer, while the target paper uses compositional variation of Al in an AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy coating. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (barrier layer vs. alloy composition change).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions normal operation at ~300°C and accident conditions at ~1000°C in steam, while the target paper tests isothermal oxidation at 1000°C and 1100°C in flowing steam. The high-temperature steam regime is broadly similar, but the hypothesis lacks the specific 60 min/30 min durations and the 1100°C test, and includes a 300°C condition not in the target.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a physical diffusion barrier to suppress Cr-Zr intermetallic formation. The target paper's mechanism involves formation of a protective Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 oxide layer that suppresses oxygen diffusion, with excess Al causing detrimental intermetallics. These are different classes of mechanisms (diffusion barrier vs. oxide scale protection).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced interdiffusion and improved coating integrity relative to an unmodified Cr coating. The target paper predicts and finds an optimum Al content (~10 at.%) that minimizes oxidation and oxygen penetration, with higher Al reversing the benefit. The predicted property (interdiffusion/corrosion resistance) and direction (improvement) are only generally aligned, but the specific outcome (Al content optimization vs. CrN barrier effect) differs substantially.
